findings.problem: load_metrics fuses file I/O (fs::read_to_string), parsing, println! logging, and domain Record construction in one function, violating Data/Calculations/Actions architecture. Shell I/O leaks into the core.
findings.failure_mode: The function cannot be tested without a filesystem, cannot be composed with alternative data sources, and printf-side-effects leak into pure domain logic making the calculation path non-deterministic.
findings.fix: Split into a shell function that handles fs::read_to_string and println!, and a pure parse_metrics(input: &[&str]) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> that consumes trusted text with no I/O.

findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() is a panic surface. unwrap() on Result from file I/O aborts the process on any file-not-found, permission-denied, or I/O error.
findings.failure_mode: An absent or unreadable metrics file causes a full process panic instead of returning a typed error that a caller can handle gracefully.
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>, propagate the I/O error with map_err(|e| LoadError::Io(e)), and define LoadError::Io(io::Error) or LoadError::NotFound.

findings.problem: parts[1] performs unchecked index access on a Vec produced from split(','). If a line has fewer than 2 comma-separated fields, this panics with index out of bounds.
findings.failure_mode: Malformed input (e.g. a single-field line) crashes the entire pipeline instead of returning a typed parse error for that record.
findings.fix: Replace parts[1] with line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid)?.1 and parse the value directly, avoiding the intermediate parts vector entirely.

findings.problem: as u16 after parse::<u32>() is a lossy cast. Values in the range 65536..=u32::MAX silently truncate to u16::MAX, losing data with no error.
findings.failure_mode: A metric value of 70000 silently becomes 4464 (70000 - 65536), corrupting data silently without any validation or error.
findings.fix: Replace as u16 with u16::try_from(parsed).map_err(|_| ParseError::ValueOutOfRange), returning a typed error for out-of-range values.

findings.problem: let parts: Vec<String> = line.split(',').map(|part| part.trim().to_string()).collect() materializes an intermediate Vec<String> just to access parts[0] and parts[1]. This is unnecessary allocation for a fixed two-field record.
findings.failure_mode: Every input line allocates a temporary Vec plus two String allocations, increasing GC pressure and memory traffic with zero benefit over streaming access.
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid)? to get (_name, value_str) directly, then parse value_str without any intermediate collection.

findings.problem: load_metrics has no bounded allocation: no domain cap on max records, no try_reserve, and no max_rows validation. The function will allocate unbounded memory from any file.
findings.failure_mode: A maliciously large file (e.g., 10GB) triggers unbounded Vec growth and OOM, causing a denial-of-service without any graceful allocation failure path.
findings.fix: Accept a max_records parameter, validate it as a positive cap, then use Vec::new() followed by out.try_reserve(max_records).map_err(|_| LoadError::Allocation)? before any push.

findings.problem: Record uses raw primitives (String for name, u16 for value) with pub fields. There is no parse boundary: callers can construct invalid domain states (empty name, negative value, overly long names) directly.
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can create Record { name: String::new(), value: 0 } or Record { name: "a".repeat(1000), value: 0 }, bypassing all domain invariants without parsing through a smart constructor.
findings.fix: Make Record fields private, add a private name newtype (struct Name(String)), and provide Record::new(name: Name, value: u16) -> Result<Self, RecordError> with validation, or use a parse method that consumes raw strings fallibly.

findings.problem: No benchmark, profiler, or allocation evidence exists for load_metrics. Without measured workload data, performance characteristics (per-iteration allocations, throughput, latency) are unverified.
findings.failure_mode: Performance claims or optimizations for this function would be unmeasured folklore. The intermediate Vec<String> per-line and println! side-effect could dominate runtime in real workloads.
findings.fix: Add a criterion or custom benchmark measuring allocations/iter, throughput (records/sec), and latency for realistic input sizes. Include a baseline of the current implementation to compare against any fix.

The source contains 7 BLOCKER violations: hidden I/O fusing shell and core, unwrap panic surfaces, unchecked indexing, lossy as cast, unnecessary intermediate Vec allocation, unbounded allocation without try_reserve/domain cap, and missing parse boundary for domain types. All absolute laws in SKILL.md section 2 are violated. The function cannot be used in any production context without these blockers being fixed.
